title: Phases of the Moon
examples: Does the Moon make its own light?
How long does one full cycle take?
What is the difference between a crescent and a gibbous?

explain.say: The Moon does not actually make its own light.

items: It needs the Sun to shine

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the phases of the Moon. Look at the sunlight, the earth and the new moon. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
We see the Moon change shape because of its orbit.
When the Moon is new, we cannot see it at all.
A crescent moon shows a little sliver of light.
The first quarter shows exactly one quarter of the Moon lit.
A gibbous moon shows more than half lit up.

faq.q: Why does the Moon change shape?
faq.a: The Moon changes shape because it orbits the Earth, and we see different amounts of sunlit side.
asks: Why does the Moon look different every night?

faq.q: How long does the whole cycle take?
faq.a: The cycle of phases takes approximately one month to complete.
asks: Is it always the same time?
How many days for a full cycle?

faq.q: What is the difference between full and new?
faq.a: During a full moon, the entire face visible from Earth is lit. At the new moon, the side lit by the Sun faces away from us.
asks: When is the Moon completely dark?
What does 'full' mean for the Moon?

faq.q: What is the difference between crescent and gibbous?
faq.a: A crescent is a small sliver, while a gibbous is more than half lit up.
asks: Can you show me a small sliver?
Is gibbous bigger than a quarter?

faq.q: Does the Earth block the light sometimes?
faq.a: Yes, the Earth's shadow can sometimes affect how we view the Moon.
asks: Does the Earth hide the Moon?
Can the Earth block the Moon's view?

facts: The Moon does not produce its own light.
The Moon orbits the Earth in a cycle.
The full moon happens when the Earth is between the Sun and Moon.
The new moon happens when the Moon is between the Earth and Sun.

quiz.say: When the Moon is completely visible and bright, what phase is it?
quiz.why: This is correct because the entire side facing Earth is lit by the Sun.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the New Moon means the Moon is not visible.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a crescent is only a small sliver of light.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the Quarter Moon means only a quarter is lit.

quiz.say: If the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun, what phase is it?
quiz.why: This is correct because the side lit by the Sun faces away from Earth.

wrong.0: This is wrong because a crescent is a visible sliver, not invisible.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a Full Moon means Earth is between the Sun and Moon.
wrong.3: This is wrong because gibbous means more than half is lit.

quiz.say: If you see more than half of the Moon lit, what phase is it?
quiz.why: This is correct because gibbous means more than half the Moon is illuminated.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the quarter phase is exactly half lit.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the New Moon means no light is visible.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a crescent is a very small amount of light.
